cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: refining what you can tell apart
cells.ask: offer the practice a season of persistent building — build the same thing again tomorrow, and let the insight that arrives be one that clears what actually needed clearing.
cells.core:
You're sharpening your sense of what matters and what doesn't — quietly, privately, without needing anyone to watch. What's arriving now is meeting a mind that can sort it, and the sorting isn't restless; it's the useful kind, the kind that knows which thing to pick up. That steadiness is free to feed something bigger: practice that keeps going, building on itself.

The refinement is real. So is the ground it's standing on.
cells.sheetLine: You can tell what matters from what doesn't, right now, without forcing it.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.place: at a door you're trying to open before it's your turn
cells.ask: let one thing finish in front of someone who can see it was done — say what the work cost you, out loud, to one person who will hear it right, and let the release come from the finishing itself.
cells.core:
You're already analyzing what hasn't come through the door yet. Every possible version gets tested, compared, refined — and the refining has stopped serving the arrival. You're bracing for a future you can't write into, and the bracing is spending the very attention that would meet it well.

What the sharpening is for is the moment in front of you. That moment is getting crowded out by the next one.
cells.sheetLine: You're solving the next thing before this one has landed.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.ask: let one thing you've been holding come out sideways — say it before it's shaped, to one person, and let what they give back count as part of the work.
cells.core:
You've been doing the careful mental work in private, and the bringing-forward stopped. The door is behind you now; you're still standing at it, refining distinctions no one has seen. It isn't that the thinking stopped — it's that thinking has become a place to stay instead of a thing to carry in.

What's missing isn't the practice. It's the exchange that would tell you which parts matter to anyone but you.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the work at the door instead of walking it through.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: already sorting, calling it something else
cells.ask: name one thing you've been calling obvious or routine as the result of your own careful seeing — and let the satisfaction of having imagined it well be yours.
cells.core:
You're already making the distinctions that shape what comes next — you pick what deserves attention, what gets let go, what gets built on — but you describe it as just how things are. The sharpening is running; the credit for it isn't claimed. People around you can feel that you know what matters. You've been letting that read as situation instead of skill.

The seeing is yours. The credit has been parked somewhere else.
cells.sheetLine: You're already choosing what matters. You just haven't called it choosing.

flags.detail: "at some point you" — a cell knows no one's past
